about.title: San Diego Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Car crashes are the most common way people are seriously hurt in San Diego, and the aftermath moves fast — the insurer may call within hours, long before you know how badly you're injured. California gives most crash victims two years to file a claim, and it uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can recover even if you were partly to blame. Recoverable losses can include medical bills, lost wages, vehicle damage, and pain and suffering, which California does not cap in ordinary crash cases. Evidence — skid marks, dashcam and traffic-camera footage, vehicle data — can disappear quickly on San Diego's busiest roads, so acting early tends to strengthen a claim. LawProactive connects injured San Diego drivers, passengers, riders and pedestrians, at no cost, with an independent car accident attorney. You pay no fee unless the case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why acting early matters after a crash

items.title: Two-year California deadline
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file, and shorter deadlines apply when a government vehicle or road is involved. Sooner is stronger.

items.title: Partial fault still recovers
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault you can recover even if you were partly responsible; your compensation is simply reduced by your share.

items.title: Don't talk to the adjuster alone
items.desc: Early recorded statements and quick offers routinely undervalue claims. An attorney can handle the insurer so you can focus on healing.

items.question: What should I do first after a car accident in San Diego?
items.answer: Get medical care, document the scene and any injuries, exchange information, and avoid giving the other insurer a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Prompt medical treatment also protects your health and your claim.

items.question: What if the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: You can still recover. California uses pure comparative fault, so your award is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated, even if you were mostly to blame.

items.question: What will it cost me?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. The review is free and car accident attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no attorney fee unless they recover compensation for you.
